items.item: `Sources/Kernel File/Kernel.File.Open.swift`: a handle resolved to `.uncached` on Darwin gets
items.reason: Needs other repositories and Darwin, which can't be checked here. The `.noCache` option (swift-darwin-standard, rawValue 1 << 30) is never turned into fcntl(F_NOCACHE): its `needsNoCache`/`openFlags` helpers are unused, and swift-iso-9945's ISO_9945.Kernel.File.Open._open passes options.rawValue straight to Darwin.open, so bit 0x40000000 (O_EXEC on Darwin, as I recall) would reach open(2). Inserting `.noCache` for `.uncached` here would therefore likely make every uncached open fail rather than fix it. The fix belongs in swift-iso-9945's Darwin open (strip the bit, then fcntl(fd, F_NOCACHE, 1)), then a one-line `resolved == .uncached` change in Sources/Kernel File/Kernel.File.swift. Darwin has no F_GETNOCACHE to inspect the descriptor in a test.

items.item: `Sources/Kernel File/Kernel.File.Open.swift`: a failed cache-mode resolution silently fall
items.reason: Resolution throws only for strict requests (.direct, .uncached, .auto(.errorOnViolation)); .auto(.fallbackToBuffered) already returns .buffered. Kernel.File.open now throws Open.Error.platform(Error(code: .ENOTSUP)) instead of silently opening buffered. ENOTSUP was chosen so the thrown type stays the same. Tests: `open with .direct the platform cannot honour throws ENOTSUP` (Linux+Darwin) and, Linux only, `open with .auto(.errorOnViolation) and unknown alignment throws ENOTSUP`. README updated.

items.item: `Sources/Kernel File/Kernel.File.Handle+writeAll.swift`: an interruption after a partial
items.reason: writeAll(from:) retries EINTR once any byte is written and throws .right(.occurred) only when nothing was written, so a thrown Interrupt always means the whole call can be repeated. Documented with ///; README updated. No regression test: EINTR after a partial write can't be triggered deterministically without signal-handler fault injection.

Linux.Kernel.IO.Uring (swift-linux-foundation/swift-linux-standard) maps the CQ ring privately and has no public accessor for the kernel's overflow counter (params.cqOff.overflow), so it can't be read from here. Removing the property from the driver instead is a public API removal and the owner's decision. Its only users are swift-kernel's own tests. Needs a public overflow accessor on Linux.Kernel.IO.Uring; then the fix here is `overflowCount: { state.overflow }`.

items.item: Expose the narrow L2 operation needed by the generic factory, write the buffer-group ID whenever bufferSelect is requested, and test that the generated SQE carries both
items.reason: Still true at Sources/Kernel Completion/Kernel.Completion+IOUring.swift (bufferSelect branch, around line 202). Submission.bufferGroup already exists, but the SQE's `_bufferGroup` setter in swift-linux-foundation/swift-linux-standard (Linux.Kernel.IO.Uring.Submission.Queue.Entry.swift:208) is @usableFromInline internal. The only public path, read(target:length:offset:bufferGroup:data:), also changes the opcode to multishot read. The acceptance asks to expose an L2 operation in that other repository, for example a public `bufferGroup` property on Entry. Then the fix here is `uring.next.entry.bufferGroup = .init(rawValue: submission.bufferGroup.underlying)` next to the `.bufferSelect` insert.

api_changes: Behaviour: Kernel.File.open(_:configuration:) now throws .platform(Error(code: .ENOTSUP)) for .direct, .uncached or .auto(policy: .errorOnViolation) when they can't be resolved (before: opened buffered). On Linux, .direct always throws today, because Requirements are always .unknown.
Behaviour: Kernel.File.Handle.writeAll(from:) no longer throws Interrupt after a partial write.
dependents: No callers outside swift-kernel's own tests pass a cache mode to Kernel.File.open or call writeAll (searched all of repos/).
notes: Not built (per brief); swift-format run and the changed test file parse-checked. Linux-only and Darwin-only paths are unverified here.
